graphEvents.label: Generated files never count as customizations
User-modified registry/router is a decision-managed unit
No order derivation from the installed set

label: What an install/update cycle ships and records: a copied or freshly installed tree reports baseRecording.needed; record-base writes .skilled/release/base.json under the apply lock with a nearest-release check; bare /doctor:update runs the read-only check; align never writes outside its ignored run directory.

Generated-versus-hand-written is an explicit policy: leaf manifests, the trigger index and its sidecars, compiled-route activation manifests and graph-metadata derived blocks never count as customizations; hub-router.json and mode-registry.json are absent from that list, so they are authored configuration shipped as ordinary unit files.

A user-modified hub registry/router/manifest is an ordinary unit file under the align/decisions machinery: decisions are adopt-release, keep-local, merge, use-proposal; apply without --decisions uses the newest alignment run at the current HEAD and writes only update and new units, re-verifying each local file against its base; customized units still need align and a --decisions file.

Deletion is a first-class keep-local-able state: recommendation() maps mergeable to merge, conflicting to use-proposal, deleted-locally/deleted-in-release/symlink-parent to keep-local, local-only/kept-local to keep-local, and take-release with customized status to adopt-release.

align and rollback keep strict mutation boundaries: align records decisions for customized, conflicting and removed units in an ignored run directory and never writes outside it; rollback restores only engine-validated paths from rollback.json and never runs git restore.

No derivation from the installed set: the update engine's unit universe is tree paths plus recorded base paths and it computes per-unit file status, not routing order; the surface rank stays authored data (hub-router.json:7, carried) copied verbatim by the mint (carried); order cannot be derived purely from what is installed.

The engine has no example-unit concept: the string example occurs exactly once in release-update.cjs and it is prose in OPTION_REMEDY; obsidian/webflow ship as ordinary units and deleting them is a normal removed unit reviewed by align.
The update docs' external-user path covers only the v3-to-v4 layout move; no /doctor:update doc distinguishes example surfaces or tells a user the two packets are deletable or replaceable.

No operator-specific configuration layer exists: decisions apply uniformly to any checkout and the only carrier for a different order downstream is a keep-local decision on a customized hub-router.json; the operator keeps its order by authoring the release-source file, so a shipped default that assumes the examples are gone changes the operator's file too unless a keep-local process is adopted.

direction: Deriving surface order from the installed packet set inside /doctor:update
